documents: Engelhardt et al. 2022, Chemical Geology 608, 121038 (published paper, PDF)

entry.evidence: The aim of this work is to provide supporting evidence that the ocean floor around the Azores is indeed hydrothermally active

steps.action: Took from Schmidt et al. (2019, 2020) the pore-water major-element anomalies that indicate deep-sea hydrothermal systems around the Azores Plateau.
steps.quote: indicates the existence of submarine hydrothermal systems located far off the MAR

steps.action: Posed the question of how the potentially hydrothermal fluids are transported through the pelagic sediments.
steps.quote: little is known about the transport mechanisms of these (potentially) hydrothermal fluids through the sediments

steps.action: Stated the working hypothesis that the Azores ocean floor is hydrothermally active, so that mantle fluids should be present in the pore water.
steps.quote: to provide supporting evidence that the ocean floor around the Azores is indeed hydrothermally active

steps.action: Adopted published expectations: pore-water Ne-Xe at air-saturated-water levels, mantle helium enriched in 3He, MORB 3He/4He of about 6.5-9.5 RA, and radiogenic 4He from U and Th.
steps.quote: mantle is known to be enriched in isotopically light helium

steps.action: Selected two coring sites on cruise M141/1 at different distances from the Terceira Rift and the MAR, both with hydrothermal-type major-element gradients reported by Schmidt et al. (2020).
steps.quote: The second sampling site (Pico/Faial), located between the islands of Pico, Faial and Sao Jorge, lies on the Terceira Rift

steps.action: Took gravity cores, sealed sediment in copper tubes using the group's established protocols, centrifuged the pore water, measured He-Xe and 3He/4He by static mass spectrometry, and measured U and Th by gamma spectroscopy.
steps.quote: noble gas analysis was performed with static mass spectrometry

steps.action: Fitted the unfractionated air model (ASW at fixed in-situ T and S, plus an air excess A) to He-Xe to separate atmospheric and terrigenic helium.
steps.quote: with the unfractionated air model

steps.action: Compared atmospheric noble gases with the calculated ASW reference; attributed supersaturation (largest for Ne) to air contamination during sampling and low Xe to incomplete degassing.
steps.quote: At both sampling sites, the concentrations of Ar, Kr and Xe are close to the calculated concentrations of ASW in the Azores region.

steps.action: Compared the terrigenic He, terrigenic 3He and 3He/4He depth profiles with the atmospheric expectation: they are zero or atmospheric at the top and rise with depth to about 9 RA, more steeply at Faial/Pico.
steps.quote: Our data show that at both sampling sites a terrigenic helium component is present in the sediment pore water

steps.action: Kept the claim that mantle helium, and therefore hydrothermal fluid, is present in the sediment pore space at both sites.
steps.quote: mantle helium is present in the sediment pore space

steps.action: Proposed, from the shape of the depth gradients, that upward transport of mantle solutes is mainly diffusion-controlled.
steps.quote: the upward transport of mantle-derived solutes is mainly diffusion-controlled

steps.action: Assuming comparable sediment transport properties, read the steeper Faial/Pico gradient as a larger 3He flux, linking hydrothermal activity to the rift and ridge spreading centres.
steps.quote: hydrothermal activity in the Azores region is linked to the rift dynamics

steps.action: Noted that near-interface pore water is close to atmospheric and inferred that the mantle signal would not appear in the bottom water.
steps.quote: evidence for hydrothermal activity might only be detectable in the sediment in the Azores region

steps.action: From the 3He gradient still present at the Southern Plateau, about 100 km from the rift, refined the transport picture to non-localized migration over large areas.
steps.quote: hydrothermal fluids migrate through the pelagic sediments over large areas of the ocean floor in a rather non-localized manner

steps.action: Fitted a two-component mixing line of 3He/4He against Ne/He for the Pico/Faial samples and extrapolated to Ne/He = 0 to estimate the source 3He/4He.
steps.quote: of about 8.6 ± 0.3 RA for noble gas data of Pico/Faial

steps.action: Interpreted the source ratio as a MORB source of the pore fluids.
steps.quote: This isotope ratio is characteristic for a MORB source

steps.action: Compared the source ratio with published 3He/4He of thermal waters and gas emissions on Pico and Faial (Jean-Baptiste et al., 2009).
steps.quote: have been found in thermal waters and gas emissions on the islands of Pico and Faial

steps.action: Refitted the mixing line on data not corrected for air excess to test whether the source estimate depends on the air correction.
steps.quote: fitting the uncorrected values in the same manner yields a similar value of 8.1 ± 0.4 RA

steps.action: Explained the lower Southern Plateau ratios by a lower 3He flux plus some radiogenic He, using the higher Th (and U) in that core and published Sao Miguel data.
steps.quote: Th concentrations at the top and bottom of the core are considerably higher in the sediments of the Southern Plateau

steps.action: Compared the Azores ratios with the Guaymas Basin black-smoker sediment study (Horstmann et al., 2021) and the Nankai Trough study, attributing the difference to the type of fluid transport.
steps.quote: as the isotope ratio found in a similar noble gas study in deep-sea sediments very close to a currently active black smoker

steps.action: Proposed that ash layers and fast bottom-water exchange explain why hydrothermal fluids do not accumulate in the bottom water.
steps.quote: could be attenuated around the Azores, due to ash layers from volcanic eruptions

steps.action: Concluded ongoing hydrothermal activity with MORB-type He and mainly diffusive, non-localized upward migration; noted that advection along faults at depth cannot be excluded.
steps.quote: These data point to ongoing hydrothermal activity in the pelagic sediments in this region

No; terrigenic and mantle He inferred via air-model separation
Support hydrothermal activity and characterize fluid transport mechanism
Partly: atmospheric-only He, radiogenic He, and diffusive versus advective transport
Mantle He predicts elevated 3He/4He toward MORB; atmospheric or radiogenic He does not
Conditions found: two cores at different distances from the rift

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: Two sites only; same pattern at both
Source ratio robust to the air correction (8.6 vs 8.1 RA)
Kept: MORB-type mantle He present; diffusive transport assumed

end.claim: Pore fluids of pelagic sediments around the Azores contain mantle helium with a MORB-type signature (source about 8.6 RA) that increases with depth, pointing to ongoing hydrothermal activity with mainly diffusive, non-localized upward fluid migration.

decisive_move.sentence: Separating the terrigenic He component from atmospheric and air-contamination components with the unfractionated air model fitted to all noble gases is what makes the mantle-helium signal visible.

gates.evidence: The sites were chosen where Schmidt et al. (2020) had reported hydrothermal-type gradients, so the hydrothermal hypothesis partly directed sampling, though the cores came from a broader cruise (p. 3). The presence of mantle He could have failed (terrigenic 3He could have been zero, the ratio atmospheric or radiogenic). Diffusive transport is assumed from the gradient shapes and not tested against advection (pp. 5-6). Nothing is stated as fixed before the data.

imports.item: Gamma spectroscopy for U and Th concentrations
Noble-gas solubility data for air-saturated water

limits: Sub-claims at other statuses: the source 3He/4He of 8.6 ± 0.3 RA is an estimate_with_resolution (p. 6). Diffusion-controlled transport is an assumption read from gradient shapes and rests on comparable sediment transport properties, which were not measured (p. 5); advection is explicitly not ruled out (p. 6). The claims that the signal is undetectable in bottom water, that migration is non-localized, and that activity is linked to the rift are inferences (pp. 5-6). Bottom water itself was not sampled; that claim rests on the shallowest pore-water samples (inference). Only two 5 m cores were taken, and no flux is quantified. Internal inconsistency: Results and Figure 4 give a maximum of about 9 RA, while p. 6 cites 'maximum value of about 5 RA' from Table 1, apparently mixing uncorrected and terrigenic ratios (inference). The Table 1 caption cites Kipfer et al. (2000), whereas the text cites 2002. Samples affected by air contamination and incomplete degassing are kept in the analysis, with large errors. No review file was supplied, though the paper thanks two anonymous reviewers, so no review sequence is coded.

disagreements.target: Horstmann et al. (2021), Guaymas Basin pore-water noble gases near an active black smoker
disagreements.support: The Azores ratios are twice as high despite no known vents, which the authors attribute to non-localized diffusive transport rather than proximity to vents.
disagreements.quote: as the isotope ratio found in a similar noble gas study in deep-sea sediments very close to a currently active black smoker

disagreements.target: The practice of inferring absence of hydrothermal activity from absent bottom-water signals
disagreements.support: The mantle He signature in pore water vanishes toward the sediment/water interface, so bottom water would not record it.
disagreements.quote: the absence of hydrothermal signals in ocean bottom water generally does not exclude the presence of hydrothermal fluids in the sediment column

alternatives_considered.reason: To test whether the accuracy of the air correction matters for the source ratio

alternatives_considered.chosen: Noble-gas supersaturation interpreted as air contamination during sampling
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Natural supersaturation (implicit: pore water is otherwise at atmospheric equilibrium)
alternatives_considered.reason: Pore water in ocean sediments is typically known to be in atmospheric equilibrium; sampling difficulties on board

alternatives_considered.chosen: Mainly diffusive transport of mantle solutes
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Advective hydrothermal transport, including along fissures and faults at depth
alternatives_considered.reason: Concentration gradients of terrigenic He with depth; results only cover the uppermost meters

alternatives_considered.chosen: Lower Southern Plateau 3He/4He mainly from a lower 3He flux
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Radiogenic He accumulation (judged to act to a lesser extent)
alternatives_considered.reason: Higher Th, and slightly higher U, in Southern Plateau sediments
